title: The king who became a seer
hookLine: a king tried to seize a sage's wish-granting cow, lost everything, and became the seer of the Gayatri
carry: the gayatri asks god to light the mind
tomorrow: who is Savitr, the god the Gayatri calls?
last: A GIVING THAT FEEDS THE NEXT GIVING.

lines: A KING, AN ARMY, A HERMITAGE.
A COW THAT GIVES WHATEVER IS ASKED.
cards: A king rides through a forest with his whole army. A sage in a hermitage feeds every last soldier a feast, and the king asks how. A cow, the sage says: a cow that gives whatever is asked.
The king decides he has to have her. He'll lose almost everything he tries next, and come out of it as one of the most honored seers in Hindu memory, the one tradition credits with the Gayatri.
Today: the seer behind the verse.

teach.h: SEER: VISHVAMITRA. METER: GAYATRI. GOD: SAVITR.
teach.b: Before many Hindus chant the Gayatri, they name three things: its seer, Vishvamitra; its meter, gayatri; its god, Savitr. In the Ramayana, Vishvamitra is born a king, not a priest.
The sage is Vasishtha, and the cow is Shabala. The king offers thousands of cows for her, elephants, gold. Vasishtha says no.
So the king takes her by force, and the cow fills the field with warriors who beat his army. He goes away, wins divine weapons through hard practice, and comes back.
Every one of them falls into the sage's wooden staff and vanishes.
And the king says, in paraphrase: a warrior's strength is nothing; a seer's strength is real. He walks away into tapas, years of hard practice. He stumbles, into anger, into desire, and begins again.

teach.h: TAPAS, AND A SEER AMONG SEERS.
teach.b: At last Vasishtha himself greets him as a brahmarshi, a seer among seers.
Tradition names him as the rishi who saw the Gayatri, and it sits in the Rig Veda's third book, the book of his family, partway through a hymn, the first verse to Savitr. Now listen to what it asks.
Not for a cow, an army or a kingdom.

Dhiyo yo nah prachodayat: may he stir our thoughts. Many teachers read the story and the verse together. The man who grabbed for a wish-granting cow is remembered for a prayer that asks only for light in the mind.
That's the heart of the Gayatri: before anything else, ask God to help you see clearly.

how: Hindus who keep the practice recite the Gayatri at dawn and dusk or with a mala, and many first name its seer, meter and god: Vishvamitra, gayatri, Savitr. In Vedic recitation it is learned as part of Rig Veda 3.62.

games.q: what does “the gayatri in context” mean?
o: a curse Vasishtha laid on the king's army
a prayer for light from a king who became a seer
a war song Vishvamitra sang to win back the cow

games.q: the seer's story — tap the pairs.
p: the king who became a seer
the sage with the wish-granting cow
the cow who fed an army

s: the Gayatri asks for wealth and victory
it asks Savitr to stir our thoughts: light for the mind, and for all of us, not one.
tradition names Vishvamitra as the seer of the Gayatri
and the Rig Veda's third book, where it sits, is the book of his family.
he was born a king, and became a brahmarshi through long tapas.

games.q: you're Vishvamitra. your army is beaten and your weapons vanished into a sage's staff. what now?
o: a seer's strength is the real one; go do tapas
games.why: a warrior's strength is nothing, he says; a seer's strength is real. years of tapas later, Vasishtha greets him as a brahmarshi.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you want badly right now: a result, a yes, someone's approval. Hold it for a breath, then set it down beside you, like a king setting down his weapons. Now ask for one thing only, clear sight.

If your tradition welcomes you to say the Sanskrit, say dhiyo yo nah prachodayat softly; if not, may our minds be lit is enough. Notice it says our, not my, and let the circle widen to the people around you.

wordCard.voice: The Gayatri in context. Rig Veda three, sixty-two, ten, in the book of Vishvamitra's family, the seer tradition names for the verse. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: thought, insight, the mind's seeing; in the Gayatri it appears as dhiyo, our thoughts, which Savitr is asked to stir.

carryVoice: Your line: the Gayatri asks God to light the mind. Vishvamitra wanted a cow, and learned to ask for light. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Rig Veda 3.62 (the hymn turns from god to god; verse 10 is the first to Savitr); Rig Veda book 3, the family book of Vishvamitra, whom the tradition names as the verse's seer
Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda (Vishvamitra, Vasishtha and the cow Shabala; the king's defeat, his tapas, and his recognition as a brahmarshi)
